title: 1.4.14 Three Structures, Three Examples
description: Name the three structures of structured programming and give an everyday example of each. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.rubricTitle: Three Structures, Three Examples — AI-graded rubric
aiGrader.prompt:
1. Name the three structures that structured programming says every program can be built from.

2. For each one, give a one-sentence example from ordinary life - not from code. Making toast, getting to school, a game you play, a chore you do. The example should make it obvious which structure it is.

3. Structured programming also forbids arbitrary jumps between parts of a program. In one or two sentences, why was giving that up worth it?

rubric.title: All three structures are named
rubric.description: Student names sequence, selection and repetition. Accept close synonyms - 'choice' or 'branching' for selection, 'loop' or 'iteration' for repetition. Credit requires all three. Naming two does not earn this criterion.

rubric.title: Each example comes from ordinary life
rubric.description: All three examples are drawn from everyday activity rather than code. Deny if the student illustrates a structure with an if statement or a for loop instead of a real-world situation, or if fewer than three examples are given.

rubric.title: Each example actually matches its structure
rubric.description: The sequence example is genuinely steps in order; the selection example genuinely involves choosing between paths based on a condition; the repetition example genuinely involves doing something more than once. Deny if any example is mismatched - for instance, a plain list of steps offered as the repetition example.

rubric.title: Explains why forbidding arbitrary jumps was worth it
rubric.description: Student says something about being able to follow or reason about the program - that you can tell how execution reached a line, that code becomes readable, that it prevents tangled flow. Deny if the answer only asserts it is 'better' or 'cleaner' without saying what it makes possible.
